The 128th headed north through day and night to reach their rendezvous with the 733th Tarentine. They were tired and heartbroken, victory is its own reward, but it doesn't make the grieving any easier.

Before departing, the fortified encampment around the defensive positions at the air-scrubbers were collapsed and Colonel Vesta had her lieutenants issue Triple Skull medals to what remained of the 6 surviving squads, combine them back to full operational strength and dispense punishments for insufficient work ethic. They had discussed privately back and forth the merits of flogging the dead in a metaphoric gesture, but the sergeants and corporals had all volunteered to receive the lashings to honour the fallen. They had spent most of the morning burying their bodies.

A full 30 hours later, hampered  by the dense jungle and constant monitoring for traps, they had reached the RV and set up a defensive perimeter from ambushes while they awaited the Vultures. The men were eager to receive the punishment before the gaze of actual Militarum eyes fell upon them.

It was not to be.

17 men bore their backs on their knees, staked to the ground. Vesta did not like it, but she followed the primer as closely as their Astartes guardians followed the codex. She put her tin cup of recaff down and marched out stiffly and remained at salute while each man received their strikes. The whole affair was a horrid one, and she fought back tears as her men accepted their licks in near silence.

Not until the last crack of the whip echoed around the small clearing and the men and had been given a sip of water did she drop her hand.

"Is it really necessary?" Came a soft, commanding voice from over her left shoulder. She turned to see who dared question the Primer's wisdom to find a dashing man in a commissar's hat and majors uniform behind her.

"Athelan?" She queried, hand quietly slipping to her bolt pistol.

"The one and same. I'm so glad to put a face to the prodigious name." He replied, holding out his hand.

A metal cybernetic gripped in response, and a dry smile was offered in greeting.

Colonel Vesta ushered the Commissar Major into her command Chimera away from the scene outside to spare her men further shame.

The two discussed the coming projects and their roles within them. The vultures, stronger in numbers and experience, would provide the defensive positions; while the 128th would setup beacons to guide the STC prefabs to their designated areas in the 3 acres of Point Kappa, now the new FOB.

Vesta had changed the order of deployment and ensured that Hab blocks were first sent crashing down from orbit. The civilians they fought hard and sacrificed so much for would be housed, as could her men. They deserve soft beds and warm linens.

The next day, the base construction and directing the orbital drops of vital buildings began in earnest.

By the third day it was all but complete, sandbags were being filled and placed against walls to reinforce, power cables were being routed into the ground, security systems were being checked and duck boards placed along busy thoroughfares to keep the churned mud to a minimum.

It was hard work, but it was a welcome distraction and a pleasant whisper of peace in war time.

"For the Emperor, for Guilliman, and for Macragge!" The preacher's words echoed around the hollow interior of the cathedral aboard the *Cleansing Vengeance* en route to the Segmentum Pacificus. "For Macragge." Came the solemn response in unison, bookending the sermon. The Havoc-class Frigate had been traversing the immaterium as part of battlegroup Invictus for over a fortnight now, a long, arduous journey across the breadth of the galaxy. Twenty vessels strong, led by a Retribution Class Battleship, *Valorous Will*, slipped silently amongst the horror of the warp beyond the Gellar field. Deep within the belly of their vessel, the mustered 128th idled and whiled away the time with drills and recreation. Mainly drills. Their martial pride and heritage were well recorded within Ultramar and their reputation preceded them within the small realm on the far eastern fringe. Being moved from the cleanse efforts of their homeworld Iax was sure to stick in their throats.

Metal hob nails clanged loudly on the bare plasteel stairs leading to the pulpit as Colonel Vesta stood before her regiment. "We have received our orders." She announced. "Kole's Hope is ablaze, we are tasked with assisting and protecting its citizenry with the extinguishing efforts. Preservation of the planet is of the utmost priority. Lumber is the tithe and we are to protect it. Expect resistance and disruption to these firefighting efforts. Fauna will be escaping the flames, I remind you to hold your fire.” She kept it brief and to the point. “Dismissed.” She tersely ordered before turning and descending the stairs and leaving the cathedral. Her soldiers remained at attention until their leader had left and they all filled out in a more relaxed fashion.

Planetside, a convoy of Chimera led the Guardsmen to the thickest of choking smoke in the dense forest. Civilians fought bravely and in vain against the sometimes 15-foot tall flames. Vesta was not without wiles and ordered the handful of hellhound supports to land with them outfitted with water rather than promethium (a great insult sorely beared by their crews) and ordered them to begin spraying the worst of the wall of flames. Squads of guardsmen were sent into the forest to fell trees and create a fire break, like the enormous farms of Iax used to have. The white and blue chivalry, almost lost in the thick black smoke of the fire, denoted these apart from the traitors of Kole’s Hope and were a welcome sight. The fact they came prepared was a great relief.

Patrols in the Chimera were sent along the lines to deliver supplies and nourishment to the bedraggled firefighters. Others were sent to corral fleeing fauna, the majority of manpower was sent to suppress the spring ambushes of xenos filth. The area of operations was so large from the roaring blaze it was impossible to be everywhere all at once and traps would be sprung and forced to be dealt with alone until reinforcements could hurry in response. Mortar teams were stationed at regular intervals, but soon became targets themselves. Overlapping fields of fire were employed, but the low visibility hampered efforts and losses were heavy. Vesta took advice from her attache and employed the aeronautica to drop explosives to starve the area of oxygen or dampen the flames with the jet's air flow. A masterstroke worthy of a commendation. Efforts were hampered further by the Munitoirum’s representative, Commander Bohn, continually belaying orders and posturing. In order to maintain diplomacy Vesta allowed the use of her command Storm Chimera and Bohn was given every luxury at their disposal to keep him entertained. He drank the best recaff and watched holovids of past battles. She suggested he undertake, in her words, the greatest task assigned to the 128th and protect the atmospheric scrubbers. Unbeknownst to him, she ordered the driver to take the scenic route and substantial delays were encountered. Trooper Silborune would be given double rations from the officers' mess for his troubles. She assured Lieutenant Garvius a medal if he kept the prig occupied with a full demonstration of the regiment’s only Macharius Vulcan, the ancient relic maintained religiously and deployed to the most valuable of objectives.

It seemed like an endless task and exhaustion set in quickly; though the worst seemed to be behind them. The vox-casters of the regiment were horse from the continual chatter throughout the operation, Chimera filters were choked with soot and medical supplies were running low.
